newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Malaysia market regulators ink pact.
newsitem.headline: China, Malaysia market regulators ink pact.

text.p: China and Malaysia's securities regulators on Friday signed an agreement calling for the sharing of information on market rules and enforcement.

The memorandum of understanding, signed in Beijing's Great Hall of the People, calls for exchanges of information and training between the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the Securities Commission of Malaysia.
"We also will be looking at the development of infrastructure and products," Malaysian Securities Commission chairman Munir Abdul Majid told reporters at the ceremony.
He said Chinese companies have been making direct investments in Malaysia but portfolio investments were limited.
"But we believe portfolio investments will follow where direct investments have already blazed the trail," he said.
"We must ensure there are sufficient safeguards for investors," he said.
China has also been eager to strengthen its legal framework for securities trading, and has turned to a number of countries in the region and elsewhere for guidance.

Chinese regulators said this was the seventh such cooperation accord signed with foreign stock regulators and followed pacts with the United States, Britain, Japan, Hong Kong, Australia and Singapore.
